slices.focus: Nadia wins approval for a standardized family-complexity case assignment model, moving from ad hoc to formal.
slices.summary: At the new-year planning meeting, Nadia wins approval to shift from arrival-order case assignment to a standardized family-complexity model using categories (housing barriers, benefits urgency, school enrollment complications, medical coordination, language access). She presented the dashboard plus inspection packets as evidence. She plans to draft a one-page implementation guide, calibrate complexity categories with a coworker on sample cases, and protect tight scope to avoid overloading the rollout.
open_loops: Draft one-page rule: who scores complexity, what gets reviewed, when reassignment is allowed
Pressure-test complexity categories on recent cases with a coworker
After calibration, finalize and circulate one-pager
Schedule check-in with team after first week and after one month
decisions: Nadia won leadership approval to shift case assignment from simple arrival order to a standardized family-complexity mod
